summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted with persistent left lower quadrant abdominal pain and diarrhea following incomplete recovery from a recent episode of C. difficile colitis. Despite initial treatment with vancomycin and metronidazole at an outside hospital, he remained symptomatic and unable to tolerate oral intake. Laboratory evaluation revealed mild hyponatremia, which improved with IV fluids and albumin. He was continued on oral vancomycin, with gradual symptom improvement over four days. His liver function remained stable, and home diuretics were resumed as his hydration status improved. He tolerated a regular diet, had no further vomiting or significant diarrhea, and was discharged home on a 7-week tapered course of vancomycin and a 9-week course of Saccharomyces boulardii. Follow-up was arranged with primary care, infectious disease, and hepatology.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol
